title: Towards Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning with Explainable AI: Applications in IoT Networks
venue: Kasdi Merbah University - Ouargla, Master Thesis
tldr: Explores an integrated federated learning and XAI framework for IoT networks using CNN, evaluating FedAvg, FedOpt, and FedAdam across different data distributions and synchronization modes.
problem_and_motivation: Federated learning faces challenges applying traditional interpretability techniques due to decentralized data, and tension exists between privacy-preserving techniques and human-understandable explanations for AI decisions.
approach: Deployed a CNN architecture within a federated learning environment for IoT network classification tasks.
Evaluated multiple FL strategies: FedAvg, FedOpt, FedAdam, and FedYogi under balanced, random, and skewed data distributions.
Integrated GradCAM and NormGrad visual interpretability tools to explain model predictions.
Compared synchronous and asynchronous communication modes with varying numbers of participating clients.
Analyzed the impact of differential privacy noise on model performance and interpretability.
findings: Different FL strategies show varying performance depending on data distribution and synchronization mode.
FedOpt and FedAdam can outperform FedAvg on non-IID data distributions.
GradCAM and NormGrad provide interpretable heatmaps for CNN predictions in the FL context.
Differential privacy noise degrades model accuracy but is necessary for privacy guarantees.
Asynchronous training offers communication efficiency but may reduce model convergence quality.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This thesis provides a comprehensive evaluation of federated learning strategies combined with XAI techniques for IoT environments. It demonstrates the trade-offs between privacy preservation (via differential privacy), model performance, and interpretability. The comparison of FedAvg, FedOpt, and FedAdam across varying data distributions offers practical guidance for FL deployment in privacy-sensitive domains.
directly_justifies: FedOpt and FedAdam can outperform FedAvg on non-IID data distributions.
GradCAM provides interpretable explanations in federated learning contexts.
Differential privacy noise trades off accuracy for privacy guarantees.
Asynchronous training improves communication efficiency at potential convergence cost.
limits: Evaluation on IoT/medical image data rather than financial transaction data.
Master thesis scope limits experimental breadth and statistical rigor.
No comparison with state-of-the-art secure aggregation protocols.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scan across all 14 topic domains was performed. Domain 10 (Privacy and Security) was flagged as high relevance because privacy-preserving FL with differential privacy is the core contribution. Domain 14.C (On-Device vs. Server Inference) was flagged as high because FL is fundamentally decentralized. Domain 10.C (Consent Management) received medium relevance. All other domains (1-9, 11-13) were rejected.

limitations: Evaluated on image/IoT data rather than financial transaction sequences. [unacknowledged]
Master thesis scope may limit depth of statistical analysis.
GradCAM explanations limited to CNN-based models; not applicable to tabular data.
remember_this: FedOpt and FedAdam outperform FedAvg on non-IID data distributions.
Differential privacy creates accuracy-interpretability trade-offs in FL.
GradCAM enables model interpretability in decentralized federated settings.
